symptom: PC cannot reach the router; ping to the router fails.
show_outputs:
show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/0
192.168.10.1
administratively down down
expected_fault: Router interface administratively down

symptom: Devices assigned to VLAN 10 cannot communicate because VLAN 10 is missing.
show_outputs:
show vlan brief
VLAN 10 is absent
expected_fault: VLAN 10 does not exist on the switch

symptom: PC can reach the local gateway but cannot reach the intended remote network.
show_outputs: PC default gateway is configured with the wrong address
expected_fault: Default gateway mismatch

symptom: A route to the remote network is absent from the routing table.
show_outputs:
show ip route
Remote destination network is not present
expected_fault: Missing route to the remote network

symptom: PC in 192.168.10.0/24 cannot reach a host in 192.168.20.0/24 while other traffic is permitted.
show_outputs:
show access-lists
Extended IP access list 100
10 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255
20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL blocks traffic from 192.168.10.0/24 to 192.168.20.0/24

symptom: Client cannot obtain an IP address automatically.
show_outputs:
show ip dhcp binding
(no client leases listed)
expected_fault: DHCP service/pool is unavailable, so the client cannot obtain a lease

symptom: IP connectivity works, but DNS name resolution times out.
show_outputs:
ping 192.168.50.1 -> 0% loss
nslookup example.com
Server: 192.168.50.99
DNS request timed out
expected_fault: Incorrect/unreachable DNS server configured on the client

symptom: PC uses the same IP address as the router, causing an address conflict.
show_outputs:
PC IP address: 192.168.60.1
Router interface: 192.168.60.1/24
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address / IP address conflict

symptom: PC cannot reach the remote LAN because the static route points to an incorrect next hop.
show_outputs:
show ip route
S 192.168.80.0/24 [1/0] via 10.0.1.3
Actual Router1 next hop: 10.0.1.2
ping 192.168.80.10 -> Request timed out
expected_fault: Wrong next-hop address in static route

symptom: VLAN traffic does not cross the inter-switch link because the two ends are configured inconsistently.
show_outputs: Inter-switch interfaces have mismatched trunk/access configuration
expected_fault: Trunk misconfiguration on the inter-switch link

symptom: PC can reach its default gateway but cannot reach a server in another VLAN.
topology: PC VLAN10 - Switch - trunk - Router-on-a-stick - Server VLAN30
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: VLAN 30 is not in the allowed VLAN list
expected_fault: VLAN 30 is missing from the trunk allowed-VLAN list

symptom: Clients receive DHCP addresses but cannot communicate outside their local subnet.
show_outputs: show ip dhcp pool: network 192.168.120.0/24; default-router 192.168.121.1
expected_fault: DHCP pool advertises a default gateway from the wrong subnet

symptom: OSPF is enabled on both routers, but no neighbor relationship forms.
show_outputs: show ip ospf neighbor: no neighbors; one interface is in area 1 while the neighbor is in area 0
expected_fault: OSPF area mismatch prevents adjacency

symptom: NAT is configured and the ISP link is up, but internal clients cannot access the internet.
show_outputs: show ip nat translations: none; NAT overload configured; ISP-facing interface has no ip nat outside
expected_fault: NAT outside is missing from the ISP-facing interface

symptom: Users can reach the web server by IP, but HTTP connections fail while other traffic is allowed.
show_outputs: show access-lists: deny tcp any host 192.168.140.10 eq 80 followed by permit ip any any
expected_fault: Extended ACL explicitly denies TCP port 80 to the web server

symptom: Two switches have the same VLAN, but hosts cannot communicate across the inter-switch link.
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: Switch0 native VLAN 10; Switch1 native VLAN 20; CDP reports native VLAN mismatch
expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch on the trunk endpoints

symptom: Wireless clients connect to the SSID but cannot reach devices on the local network.
topology: Laptop - Guest WiFi - Wireless Router - LAN
show_outputs: Guest Network enabled; Allow guests to access local network = Disabled
expected_fault: Guest wireless isolation prevents access to the internal/local network

symptom: A PC connected to Fa0/1 is placed in the wrong VLAN.
show_outputs:
show vlan brief
10 USERS active
20 SERVERS active Fa0/1
expected_fault: Switch access port is assigned to the wrong VLAN

symptom: A PC connected to Fa0/1 loses connectivity because the switch port is disabled.
show_outputs:
show interfaces fa0/1 status
Fa0/1 disabled
show interfaces fa0/1
FastEthernet0/1 is administratively down
expected_fault: Switch port is administratively shut down

symptom: PC cannot communicate because its subnet mask places it in the wrong network.
expected_fault: Incorrect subnet mask causes the host and gateway to be treated as being in different subnets

symptom: A switch interface is configured for the wrong duplex mode, causing communication problems and collisions.
show_outputs:
show interfaces fa0/2 status
Duplex setting does not match the connected device
expected_fault: Duplex mismatch on the switch port

symptom: The router cannot resolve a hostname because an incorrect DNS server is configured for name lookup.
show_outputs: PC can ping its gateway, but hostname lookup fails against an unreachable DNS server
expected_fault: Unreachable DNS server configured for hostname resolution

symptom: PC0 cannot reach Router0; ping fails with 'Request timed out'.
show_outputs:
show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/0
192.168.10.1
administratively down
down
expected_fault: Interface administratively down

symptom: PC1 and PC2 are on the same VLAN 10 but cannot ping each other.
show_outputs:
show vlan brief
VLAN Name      Status
1    default   active
20   Sales     active
PC1 and PC2 switchports are configured with 'switchport access vlan 10'
expected_fault: VLAN 10 does not exist on the switch

symptom: PC3 can ping other devices on its own subnet but cannot reach any remote network.
show_outputs:
show running-config
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
PC3 config: IP 192.168.20.25, Subnet 255.255.255.0, Default Gateway 192.168.30.1
expected_fault: Default gateway mismatch

symptom: New laptop on the LAN does not receive an IP address automatically.
show_outputs:
show running-config | section dhcp
ip dhcp pool LAN_POOL
 network 192.168.40.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.40.1
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip address 192.168.40.1 255.255.255.0
 shutdown
expected_fault: DHCP server interface is shut down

symptom: Devices in the branch office all receive IP addresses in the wrong subnet (169.254.x.x).
show_outputs:
show running-config | section dhcp
no service dhcp
ip dhcp pool BRANCH
 network 192.168.50.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.50.1
expected_fault: DHCP service is globally disabled on the router

symptom: Users can browse the internet by IP address but 'www.example.com' fails to resolve.
show_outputs:
show running-config | include dns
no ip domain-lookup
PC6 IPCONFIG: DNS Server: 0.0.0.0
ping 8.8.8.8 -> Success rate is 100 percent
expected_fault: No DNS server configured on client/router

symptom: Internal users report that 'intranet.company.local' resolves to the wrong IP address.
show_outputs:
show running-config | section dns
ip host intranet.company.local 10.10.10.5
Actual intranet server IP is 10.10.10.50 per topology notes
expected_fault: Incorrect static DNS host entry on router

symptom: PC8 on network 172.16.1.0/24 cannot reach a server on network 172.16.3.0/24 through two routers.
show_outputs:
show ip route (Router6)
C    172.16.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
C    172.16.2.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/1
destination network: 172.16.3.0
expected_fault: Missing route to 172.16.3.0/24 on Router6
